gold_rule: strict = the predicted SNOMED CT code is in the gold code set for that mention; CONCEPT_LESS is correct only against CONCEPT_LESS gold
gold_rule_note: CADEC gold is not always a single code: 252 mentions are post-coordinated (A + B) and 3 are disjunctions (A or B). Scoring 'in the gold set' gives credit for either half of a post-coordinated pair. 2.8% of mentions are affected; report them separately.

corpus.name: GeoWebNews
corpus.version: Gritta et al., A Pragmatic Guide to Geoparsing Evaluation, GPL-3.0
corpus._licence: GPL-3.0 — REDISTRIBUTABLE, like FiNER and unlike CADEC.
corpus._encoding_note: Gold offsets are against the UTF-8 decoding. The files round-trip byte-for-byte as latin-1, which makes latin-1 look right and shifts every offset after the first non-ASCII character. Measured: 2,399 of 2,401 offsets exact under UTF-8; the two failures are both in document 19 and are dropped, not repaired.
corpus._stratum_note: cadec_type carries the OVERLAP STRATUM — identical 40.5% / subset 24.8% / partial 4.9% / none 29.9%, from gold alone. This is the arm's independent variable.
corpus._ambiguity_note: 1,117 of 2,399 mentions (47%) have a canonical name held by more than one GeoNames entry. The pick step is disambiguation among identically-named candidates, not retrieval from a large space — a different failure mode from CADEC's.
corpus._split_note: 40 dev / 60 test, matching CADEC and FiNER so the three arms are comparable at a glance. 100 of 200 documents are used; the remaining 100 are pool. NOT stratified by overlap regime — that would stratify on the dependent variable and bias the very number this arm exists to measure.

prompts._derivation: Derived from GeoWebNews's own gold over 2,399 mentions in 200 documents, not invented. 20.7% of surface forms are multi-token; 12.7% are abbreviated or dotted (U.S., UK, EU, N.J.); 1,146 mentions are repeats of a form already tagged earlier in the same document, and every repeat is tagged separately — the same convention CADEC and FiNER have. 29.9% of surface forms share NO token with the canonical name they resolve to, which is the arm's central fact and is why the rules below say a demonym counts.
prompts.author: the article
prompts.rules:
Quote the place EXACTLY as the article writes it. If it says 'U.S.', quote
'U.S.' and not 'United States'; if it says 'Britain', quote 'Britain'.
Measured on gold: 12.7% of mentions are abbreviated or dotted forms and
20.7% run to more than one word.

A WORD THAT REFERS TO A PLACE COUNTS EVEN WHEN IT IS NOT THE PLACE'S NAME.
'French', 'Chinese', 'Russian' and 'American' each refer to a country and
are reported, quoted as written. Measured: 29.9% of gold mentions are of
this kind, so skipping them loses nearly a third of the answer.

Report a place EVERY TIME it appears. If an article names Russia eight
times, report it eight times, each one where it appears — never merge
repeats. Measured: 1,146 of 2,399 gold mentions are repeats within their
own document.

Report places, not organisations that merely contain one. 'the European
Commission' and 'the Bank of England' are institutions; the article is
still referring to a place through them, so quote what the article wrote
and let the next step decide which place it is.

A person's name, a company, a product or a nationality used as a language
('he spoke French') is not a place.
prompts.pick_guidance:
Choose the entry for the place the article ACTUALLY MEANS, which is
often not the largest or best-known one with that name.

This is the whole difficulty. Measured on gold: 1,117 of 2,399 mentions
name a place that more than one GeoNames entry shares — there are three
Parises on the menu and several Washingtons. The surrounding sentence is
what decides: a local newspaper reporting on a school board means the
small town, not the capital.

For a demonym or an abbreviation, choose the entry for the place it stands
for: 'French' is France, 'DPRK' is North Korea, 'N.J.' is New Jersey.

Where the article names an institution, choose the place it sits in.
prompts.span_question: really a place this news article refers to
prompts._span_question_note: The rung 4 judge prompt is the seventh prompt constant and was missed by the 2026-08-29 FiNER port, which left an SEC filing being asked whether a figure was something 'the writer says they EXPERIENCED'. CADEC's phrasing encodes first-person experience; a news article refers to a place rather than experiencing one. Declared here rather than defaulted, because it is a claim about this corpus's gold and not a wording preference.
prompts._claim_wording_note: Without these the judge prompt would read 'claimed a specific place WAS REPORTED, with a GeoNames place PLACE' — CADEC's claim_verb colliding with this corpus's own vocabulary noun. Only the corpus knows whether its entities are reported, filed or referred to.
prompts._negation_note: CADEC's negation rule is DROPPED, not translated, exactly as on FiNER. CADEC gold marks denied reactions with negated:true; GeoWebNews has no denied-place convention, so `negated` is always false here. Recorded because a silently dropped rule is indistinguishable from an overlooked one.
prompts._metonymy_note: NOT written into the rules, deliberately, and it will cost recall. The annotators resolved institutions to the building they sit in — Congress to United States Capitol, the Oval Office and the West Wing to the White House. That is a defensible reading of 'where' and it is invisible to any string comparison, so those mentions will land in BAND however good the model is. Left undeclared because a rule that teaches the model one corpus's annotation convention is teaching it the answer key, not the task.

vocabulary._note: GeoNames in registry.py's schema, so the SAME Registry class checks this corpus as checks CADEC. 13,463,738 places, MAIN NAME ONLY. is_active and is_finding are vacuously true — only exists and lexical_match do real work.
vocabulary._coverage: 97.8% of gold mentions resolve to an id (2,346 of 2,399). cities15000 alone would have reached 37.4% of distinct names; allCountries reaches 98.1%.

gate._note: A code this vocabulary must hold and one it must not. GeoNames ids are numeric and dense, so the fake was checked rather than assumed: exists(999999999) is False on this index.

model.temperature_note: Declared 2026-08-31 so this corpus has the same one answer to "which temperature produced this number" that manifest.json now has. manifest.model.temperature became load-bearing that day (ladder/llm.py:temperature_for); undeclared, this ran on llm.GREEDY_TEMPERATURE, which is the same 0.0 and NOT the same fact. Zero changes no FiNER number: every run in out/finer/ was produced at an effective 0.0.
model._frozen: Identical to manifest.json at phase F. NOT tuned for this corpus, deliberately. A model tuned per corpus would make the two arms incomparable, and the prompts were tuned on CADEC's dev split over five phases — so FiNER runs with prompts fitted to a different domain. State that as a limitation; do not fix it by tuning, which would forfeit the comparison.
model._judge_name_note: The ollama name carries the ibm/ namespace. Without it this said 'ollama/granite4:micro-h', which does not exist, and the first full FiNER run died at rung 4 after 133 minutes of rung 0 and rung 3 compute. The CADEC manifest always had the right name, so only a second corpus could surface it. llm.check_models now validates every model the run needs before rung 0 starts.

rung_order_note: Frozen at phase F. Not re-derived for this corpus.
rung0_mode_note: recall | search. Plan v16 §2.1 recommends 'recall' for iteration 1 — the model emits a code from memory, no tools — because that is what 'bare LLM' means and it is what makes rung 1's rejection rate meaningful. The scaffolding's template defaulted to 'search'; the A/B between them is the iteration-2 experiment, listed under `ablations`. Whichever is used, it changes what every number above it means, so it lives here.

ablations.name: rung0 search vs recall
ablations.why: POST-HOC ONLY — the search runs after generation and the model never sees it, so this measures prompt wording plus a coincidence rate, NOT tool access. A real tool loop (model calls search mid-generation) is untested and is the experiment this ablation is often mistaken for.

ablations.name: rung order
ablations.why: abstention early. Turns 'abstention should run last' from an assertion into a measurement.

ablations.name: vocabulary backend
ablations.why: the two backends disagree on 23.9% of gold; this prices that difference in rung-1 terms.

0.rung0_offsets_note: Discard the model offsets and locate span_text by string search. Measured: offsets are 19% correct at best, while the quote itself is verbatim 77% of the time.
0.rung0_step_note: S0 | S1 | S2 — the rung 0 prompt-engineering study, added 2026-08-23, FROZEN TO S2 on 2026-08-24 after the dev-split measurement. Scope is identical in all three and only where the CODE comes from changes: S0 recalls label and code from the model's weights, S1 recalls the label and resolves the code through data/keywords.csv, S2 retrieves a shortlist per mention and picks from it. Measured over 40 dev documents and 226 scorable gold reaction mentions with ollama/gpt-oss:20b at reasoning_effort=low — F1 exact / F1 overlap / calls / tokens / parse failures: S0 0.018 / 0.018 / 40 / 43,998 / 5-of-40; S1 0.171 / 0.305 / 57 / 36,079 / 0; S2 0.209 / 0.310 / 75 / 68,906 / 0. S2 wins exact F1 by 3.8 points and ties S1 on overlap within half a point, AND COSTS 1.9x THE TOKENS — that is a declared trade, not a free win, and the three cost measures carry it. S0 is not a weaker step but a broken one: an order of magnitude below the others for MORE tokens, and the only step that fails to parse, because its schema demands a nine-digit identifier the model does not have. Frozen because rungs 1-6 must all be measured against ONE rung 0 — three different ones make nothing above comparable. --rung0-step still overrides for a single run and writes the choice into the manifest copy saved beside the results. `null` is the pre-study A/B mode path, NOT 'the default step'.
0.rung0_shortlist_note: How many CONCEPTS S2 shows (deduped by code since 2026-08-25). Deduped dense recall over the 6,595 coded gold mentions: @20 87.0%, @30 88.9%, @40 90.2%, @60 91.8% — and k STAYED 20 anyway, because arm 4 (2026-08-25) measured the other side of the trade: at k=40 the pick step lost more than retrieval gained (pick-past-gold 34 -> 47, F1 exact 0.289 -> 0.236). Menu recall is not menu accuracy.
0.keyword_table_note: Where rung 0 turns a NAME into a code. Built from the SNOMED release alone by `python -m ladder.keywords --build`; nothing in it reads CADEC or the gold annotations. Findings and disorders only — resolving through Registry.resolve searched every description in the release, which is what answered |California chicken (organism)| for a rectal bleed and let |Gaseous substance| outrank the right concept for 'gas'. There is NO fallback to the registry when a name is absent: an unresolved name is unresolved, and falling back would reinstate the search this replaces and hide which of the two answered. The registry is still loaded — rung 1 needs exists/is_active/finding_status/terms over the WHOLE release, and S2's shortlist is retrieved from it.
0.rung0_retrieval_note: dense | lexical — which retriever builds S2's candidate menu. NOTE THAT THE TWO ALSO SEARCH DIFFERENT CORPORA: 'lexical' is Registry.shortlist, Jaccard token overlap over the SQLite description table (1,822,645 rows, 721,187 concepts, every semantic type, filtered to findings AFTER ranking); 'dense' is cosine over the embedded keyword table (227,554 rows, 127,515 concepts, findings and disorders, active only, filtered BEFORE ranking; granite-embedding:30m, 384 dims, local). MEASURED 2026-08-24 over the same 6,595 scorable coded gold reaction mentions, with the corpus and the scoring varied SEPARATELY — recall@20: lexical over descriptions 61.8%, lexical over keywords.csv 65.1%, dense over keywords.csv 86.1%. So embeddings are worth +21.0 points and the cleaner corpus +3.3. At k=1 it inverts (19.5% / 48.6% / 63.8%): +29.1 of corpus against +15.2 of scoring, because filtering to findings before ranking is what clears the top slot. The default moved on that and on nothing else. Two lexical defects dense removes, neither tunable: Jaccard's denominator penalises long terms, so for 'extreme rectal bleed' |Rectal| scores 0.33 and |Rectal hemorrhage| 0.25 and the wrong shorter concept wins; and there is no stemming, so 'bleed' never reaches 'bleeding'. Dense has its own failure mode and it is not hidden: 'gas' returns |gas gangrene| and its variants. Lexical stays reachable because a number produced under one retriever is only interpretable next to the other. Both return the same hit shape (i, code, label, fsn, via) so rung 0's pick logic never branches on which one ran, and the choice is written onto every record as checks.rung0_retrieval.
0.embed_prefix_note: Where the dense index lives: <prefix>.vectors.npy (float16, L2-normalised, one row per keyword) and <prefix>.rows.json (keyword,code in MATRIX ORDER). A CACHE, unlike data/keywords.csv — derived from the table by a fixed function and rebuildable in minutes, so it sits beside snomed.sqlite. REBUILD IT WHENEVER THE KEYWORD TABLE CHANGES: the loader checks the row counts agree, which catches a truncated write but not a stale matrix built from a different table of the same size.
0.rung0_fewshot_note: FLIPPED TRUE 2026-08-25 on the dev measurement (docs/decisions.md same date): the synthetic worked example is +5.7pt exact / +5.3pt overlap F1 over the frozen S2 (0.266/0.363 vs 0.209/0.310) at 1.55x the baseline tokens (106,627 vs 68,906), same call count, zero parse failures. This changes the frozen rung 0, so it was a joint manifest edit; rungs 1-6 must be measured against THIS configuration. The example is synthetic — never CADEC text, test-enforced — and False reproduces the pre-example arm.
0.rung0_fewshot_docs_note: FiNER POOL documents, rendered at runtime. Pool only, enforced upstream: a dev or test example would put its own gold answers into the prompt of a scored run. 0051 is 13 mentions over 9 distinct tags (exhaustiveness, repeated tag types); 0049 is 7 over 5. Chosen to mirror CADEC's pairing of one dense example and one moderate. CADEC's examples (ARTHROTEC.22, ARTHROTEC.110) are patient posts and do not exist here — few-shot examples belong to the CORPUS, which is the same finding as the task prompt one layer down, and it was found the same way: by pointing the harness at a second dataset.
0.rung0_trim_note: Phase B(d), 2026-08-25. Trim rung 0's spans to the answer key's boundary convention AFTER locate(): rules LEARNED AT RUNTIME from POOL gold only (ladder/trim.py; dev/test refused) - lead/trail tokens gold leaves outside a boundary >=95% of >=20 sightings, plus an interior clause cut at tokens whose inside_rate <= 2% over >= 50 occurrences ('pain that wakes me up' stops at 'that'). Thresholds measured on the baseline dev records: looser cut points bought exact F1 by cutting spans out of their overlap matches and were rejected. Effect on the phaseB-2 dev run: F1 exact 0.358 -> 0.362, overlap byte-identical; the original quote survives on every trimmed record as checks.span_untrimmed. False reproduces the untrimmed arm.
0.rung0_retrieval_note_finer: DEVIATION FROM FROZEN, declared — the second, after dense -> lexical, and with the same cause. Retrieval is a function of what is being retrieved from, and the two corpora differ by three orders of magnitude. CADEC ranks 20 candidates out of 129,675 concepts because they cannot go in a prompt. FiNER's 139 tag names can, so 'full' offers all of them and does no ranking. MEASURED CAUSE: the FiNER span is a NUMBER, so shortlist('19.8') has no tokens to overlap on and returned [] for every record — 22 of 22 came back with declined_shortlist:true and sct:null, which rung 1 correctly read as BAND rather than as a wrong code. Retrieval by term overlap is meaningless when the span carries no terms. COST: a 139-item menu on every pick call against CADEC's 20. Tokens per record will rise and that belongs in the cost column, not treated as free.
0.rung0_shortlist_k_note: 139 = the whole vocabulary, which is the point of rung0_retrieval='full'. The default of 20 is right for CADEC, where the menu is 20 of 129,675 concepts. Here it silently truncated the full menu to the first 20 tags alphabetically, identically for every record, so the right answer was almost never present and the model declined all 704 times. That looked like a finding about abstention and was a config cap.
0.rung0_drop_duplicate_spans_note: ON for FiNER. Measured on the finer-full-2 dev run: the same span key appears twice 39 times ('2:45 p.m.' x3, 'two business days' x4), costing 0 of 165 gold mentions. The arm already existed and was simply never declared here.
0.rung0_drop_datelike_note: ON for FiNER. A span that IS a bare year or a clock time is a date, not a reported quantity. Measured on finer-full-2: 22 years + 4 times among 238 false positives, 0 of 165 gold lost. Only a span that IS a date is dropped - '2018 revenues' survives. A third candidate, 'drop any span with NO DIGIT', was measured and REJECTED: 14 predictions cut but 7 gold destroyed, because FiNER spells small counts out ('two' -> NumberOfOperatingSegments). Free filters ship; the one with a false-rejection cost does not.
0._filters_note: rung0_split and rung0_cut_rate are deliberately NOT declared here: the splitter is a coordination splitter learned on clinical phrases and cut_rate tunes a trimmer whose rules are learned from POOL GOLD at runtime, and FiNER's spans are bare numbers. Porting them unmeasured would declare as measured something never measured on this corpus. rung0_drop_ungrounded and rung0_drop_fragments are also left off: ungrounded costs 1 prediction here and fragments would overlap the rejected no-digit filter. Only what was measured ON THIS CORPUS is declared.
0._fewshot_note: Two POOL documents, chosen for 3-8 mentions and under 2,500 characters. The FiNER ids arrived with the copied manifest and the pool guard refused them — an example from dev or test would put its own gold answers into a scored prompt. Caught in a 3-document smoke run, before any rented GPU time.
0._retrieval_note: Retrieval settings taken from manifest.json, NOT from the FiNER manifest this file was copied from. FiNER used rung0_retrieval='full' because 139 tags fit in a prompt; GeoNames has 13,463,738 entries and the guard in _retriever refused it. Using CADEC's settings is also the right comparison — the geo arm exists to test whether the ACCEPT lane generalises, so everything except the vocabulary should match the arm it is being compared against.
0._retrieval_deviation: DECLARED DEVIATION from manifest.json, which uses dense. Dense retrieval is cosine over the EMBEDDED KEYWORD TABLE — 227,554 rows derived from SNOMED. No such table exists for GeoNames, and building one means embedding 13,463,738 place names. So this arm uses `lexical`: Registry.shortlist, Jaccard token overlap over the description table, which works on any index. THE COST IS KNOWN AND IT IS LARGE: on CADEC, dense beat lexical by 21.0 points of recall@20 (86.1% vs 65.1%). Expect a lower ceiling here for that reason alone, and do NOT read a lower geo F1 as a property of the corpus. Same root cause as FiNER's deviation — the retriever available depends on the vocabulary's size and shape, which is itself a finding about portability.

1.mode_note: Rung 1 judges without routing. Its verdicts are recorded, counted and reported, but the record's zone is untouched, so rungs 3-6 see the full unfiltered set and each rung's marginal contribution stays attributable to that rung. Rung 2, which runs last, is where a rung 1 verdict is allowed to cost coverage. Set 'gate' to make rung 1 filter, as the plan's flow implies.
1.lexical_mode_note: exact chosen over contained by measurement: contained accepts 19.0% of planted near-miss codes vs 0.1% for exact, buying 11.4pt of ACCEPT-lane coverage. See docs/decisions.md and out/rung1_detection*.json.
1.label_check_note: off | flag | reject. Rung 0's sct_label against the vocabulary's own words for the code it chose. Catches what exists() cannot: 82249009 is real and active and means |California chicken (organism)|, which granite4:micro-h emitted for 'extreme rectal bleed'. FLAG, not reject — 'rectal bleeding' against |Rectal hemorrhage| is one concept in two wordings, and this check's false-rejection floor has not been measured. Same posture as meddra_check and negation_action, and for the same reason.
1.outdated_check_note: off | flag. A retired code SNOMED has since replaced is out of date, not invented: the model named a real concept and lacked the newer release. Rung 1 records sct_outdated and sct_replacement and NEVER rejects on them — same posture as meddra_check, negation_action and label_check. The successor comes from the association refset (SAME AS / REPLACED BY only; POSSIBLY EQUIVALENT TO and WAS A are excluded on purpose) and is scored as its own outcome in ladder/score.py, never folded into 'correct'. Measured 2026-08-24: only 27.3% of CADEC's 407 retired gold reaction mentions have such a successor at all.

3.enabled_note: DISABLED 2026-08-26 (Phase D step 1) while its sampler was repaired, RE-ENABLED the same day on the measurement. The 2026-08-25 full-ladder dev run measured 206/240 records not_resampled (votes keyed on exact (doc_id, spans), which shift between samples) and 9 of 32 rung-1-verified-ACCEPT codes OVERWRITTEN with memory-recalled hallucinations, because the sampler drew from the legacy recall prompt while rung 0's codes came from the frozen S2 retrieve-and-pick path. Repaired (all TDD'd, tests/test_r3_repair.py): votes matched by span overlap one-to-one per record identity; every sample drawn through rung 0's configured path (r0.prepare + r0.extract_document, S2 retrieve-and-pick, few-shot, trimmer); a change requires seen >= 2 (one counted vote is not a vote — the k<2 argument); documents sampled in sorted order so the draw sequence is reproducible from the run id. Re-enabled on out/phaseD-r3-2 (dev, 245 records): not_resampled 38/245, ZERO correct codes destroyed (baseline: 11), the only verified-ACCEPT change a genuine 2-1 menu-sourced majority, stack F1 exact 0.335 -> 0.347. A disabled rung remains a RECORDED state: run.py writes a 'disabled' ledger row and aggregate entry, so 'rung 3 did not run' stays distinguishable from 'rung 3 found nothing'.

4.menu_note: off | ranked | shuffled. Appended 2026-09-03 (plan item 14). Until then the judge was handed `code: <nine digits>` and no name, no menu, no pick, and asked whether it was the right SNOMED CT concept - a question it could not answer, so every published rung 4 number is a blind-judge measurement (on FiNER rec.sct IS the tag name, which is why the judge engaged there: identifier readability, not context size). With `ranked` the judge is shown the menu rung 0 retrieved (checks.candidates, rendered as rung 0 rendered it), the line the extractor chose, the [denied] marker where rung 0 claimed one, and asked a third question, `best`: the line it would choose or null for 'not on this list' - the verdict that separates a bad pick from a bad menu. `shuffled` permutes the menu per record under manifest.seed (blake2b of seed:record_id), because a judge shown a ranked list may ratify line 0; safe here, unlike rung 0's B4 arm, because the judge sees one record per call. OFF because the arm must be paired against exactly what was published; the arms are manifest.judgemenu.json and manifest.judgeshuffle.json (CADEC) and manifest.finer.judgemenu.json / manifest.finer.judgeshuffle.json (FiNER), one-key diffs pinned by tests/test_r4_menu.py. Couples rung 4 to S2 - an S0/S1 record gets the blind prompt and checks.r4_menu = 'none'.

5.tau_retired: tau RETIRED 2026-09-03 (plan item 17d). It was read - unlike the five settings the 2026-08-31 audit found dead - and it could never usefully fire: rung 0 reports >= 0.95 confidence on every record (1.0 on 77%; {1.0: 204, 0.99: 44} on dev) while being right about 40% of the time, so no threshold separates anything. A live key that is structurally inert looks tunable, which is the same defect one layer along from 'declared and never read'. ladder/rungs/r5.py REFUSES the key rather than ignoring it, its sweep went with it, and tests/test_tau_retired.py keeps every tracked manifest free of it. A calibrated abstention input (B7, registered) would be a different dial under a different name.

6.mode_note: simulated | desk. Implemented 2026-08-26 (Phase E, ladder/rungs/r6.py). The queue is rung 5's abstained residue, each record still carrying checks.withheld. 'simulated' routes the queue to ESCALATE and PRICES it at minutes_per_record — no answer is invented, coverage cannot move, and every ledger row carries human_minutes with minutes_source='simulated'; it measures the bill of stopping at rung 5, not the person. 'desk' applies a resolutions file (cfg key 'resolutions') written by a review session at scripts/r6_desk.py — decisions code|concept_less|uphold|skip, matched to records BY SPAN KEY one-to-one (never by record_id, which is a position), minutes MEASURED from seconds at the desk. Rows carry ids, offsets, codes and vocabulary labels only — never corpus text. scripts/r6_desk.py --oracle writes the file deterministically from gold: an ORACLE CEILING, labeled resolved_oracle in every ledger row and oracle:true in the aggregate, priced at the simulated rate, and REFUSED on the test split. Rung 6 takes no model — ROLE_BY_RUNG gives it no role, deliberately. Human minutes are the third cost measure and are never fused with tokens or usd.

scorer_note: Added 2026-08-23; until then the accuracy columns were written empty rather than guessed. Gold is keyed by SPAN, never by position: under index-based comparison a perfect extraction listed in another order scores 0.216. span_match is 'exact' for the headline; 'overlap' exists because rung 3 keys on exact spans and its resamples never align.
_experiment: FiNER-139 — the same ladder, a second corpus. The ONLY thing that varies from manifest.json is the corpus and the vocabulary. Rung order, rung parameters, models, thresholds and prompts are frozen at the phase F configuration, because a second data point is worth nothing if the ladder moved between them.
_why_this_corpus: CADEC's findings were all shaped by a knowledge gap: the extractor did not know SNOMED, so it fabricated codes, and every rung's bet was made against that. FiNER-139 has 139 tags. They fit in a prompt. The knowledge gap is GONE, and with it the odds on every rung change at once. That is the contrast — not replication.

_prediction._recorded_before_the_run: 2026-08-28. Written down first so the result is a measurement rather than a story told afterwards. Deciding what a run showed after seeing it is the failure this whole project documents.
_prediction.rung_1_validate: WEAKENS. 'Does the code exist' is near-trivial against 139 tags the model can see, so code_unknown should approach zero and rung 1's rejection rate should fall well below CADEC's 5.1%. The deterministic spine has less to do, which is a cost of the closed vocabulary, not a benefit.
_prediction.rung_2_repair: IMPROVES. On CADEC it declined 158 of 158 because the model had no better code to offer. Here it can be told a tag is wrong and pick from a list it can see. If repair ever works, it works here.
_prediction.rung_3_vote: UNCERTAIN, and the interesting one. On CADEC samples did not re-find the same spans, so voting had almost nothing to vote on. Numeric spans are far more stable than patient prose, so the mechanism should at least ENGAGE. Whether agreement means anything is a separate question: errors from a closed choice set are correlated differently from fabrications, and voting bets they are not.
_prediction.rung_4_judge: IMPROVES. A small judge cannot verify a SNOMED code it has never seen. It can plausibly check whether a number in a sentence is an interest rate or a face amount.
_prediction.rung_5_abstain: WEAKENS. It withdrew 242 of 314 on CADEC and that was the layer that worked. With fewer invalid answers upstream there is less to withdraw, so its contribution should shrink — which, if it happens, is the clearest evidence that abstention's value is a function of what is above it.
_prediction.if_nothing_flips: That is the stronger result, not a failed run: the ordering would be domain-independent. Say so either way.

_frozen_from.manifest: manifest.json at b7aba48 (Phase F: test split run once)
_frozen_from._note: Fill in the SHA from `git rev-parse --short HEAD` at the phase F merge before running. ladder/provenance.py records the SHA of the run itself; this records what it was frozen AGAINST. Both are needed: the ladder is under active development, and a comparison against a moving reference is not a comparison.

_inherits: manifest.json at b7aba48 (phase F), then the corpus, vocabulary, model and output blocks replaced. Everything else — rungs, gold_rule, scorer, unit_of_evaluation, ablations — is inherited UNCHANGED. An earlier version of this file carried an empty rungs block as a statement that nothing was overridden; it meant nothing was CONFIGURED, so rung 0 ran without rung0_offsets='search' and every span came back ungrounded. A manifest that says 'same as that one except these' is the only safe form.
_arm: Smoke test only — 3 documents, full ladder. Not a measurement.
